issue.title: SQLite gets confused about date types in certain CASE constructions

repository.name: ehrql
repository.description: ehrQL: the electronic health record query language for OpenSAFELY

issue.body:
As [discovered](https://github.com/opensafely-core/ehrql/actions/runs/7416510191/job/20181603781) by Hypothesis, in the following example SQLite returns a string rather than a date:
```python
# example.py

import datetime

from ehrql.query_model.nodes import (
    AggregateByPatient,
    Case,
    SelectTable,
    TableSchema,
    Value,
)
from tests.generative.test_query_model import data_setup


e0 = SelectTable("e0", TableSchema())

population = AggregateByPatient.Exists(e0)

variable = Case(
    {
        Value(False): None,
    },
    default=Value(datetime.date(2000, 1, 1)),
)

data = [
    {"type": data_setup.E0, "patient_id": 1},
]
```

```console
$ just gentest-example-run example.py

AssertionError: Mismatch between in_memory and sqlite
assert equals failed
  [                                    [                                   
    {                                    {                                 
      'patient_id': 1,                     'patient_id': 1,                
      'v': datetime.date(2000, 1, 1),      'v': '2000-01-01',              
    },                                   },                                
  ]                                    ]
```

This is specifically related to having `None` as the only non-default CASE value. Changing the example to the below gives the right type:
```py
    {
        Value(False): Value(datetime.date(1900, 1, 1)),
    },
```

Presumably this is related to the fact that SQLite doesn't actually have a date type but some combination of SQLite/the Python driver/SQLAlchemy conspire to pretend that it does and that in this particular case the conspiracy breaks down.

body: that's fine, I would have thought case() had a `type_` parameter also but apparently not.    if you can write a changelog message that is in the area of "enhanced case() to derive the ultimate type by scanning the given expressions for the first non-NULL expression, rather than hardcoding to the last WHEN case", that would be helpful.
